title: GTA 6 Ditches the Infamous Mash X Button to Sprint Mechanic
description: According to media reports, GTA 6 is finally fixing one of Rockstar's most criticized control schemes. You will no longer need to mash the X button to sprint.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## A Long-Awaited Relief: GTA 6 Won't Make You Mash the X Button to Sprint

Most of the games Rockstar Creates are considered absolute masterpieces by players and critics alike, setting gold standards for open-world design, storytelling, and attention to detail. However, if there are any consistent criticisms leveled at the studio's legendary titles over the years, it is usually not long before the control schemes are brought up for debate.

According to a recent report by gaming media outlet Push Square, one of the most notorious examples of this issue is finally being addressed in the upcoming release. For years, the demand to constantly press the X button on the controller just to make a character sprint has been a staple of frustration for players.

### Moving Away from Retro Control Choices

In previous titles, the requirement to repeatedly hammer the X button to build and maintain speed was a hallmark of Rockstar's traversal system. While players grew accustomed to it out of love for the immersive worlds, it remained a frequent target of jokes and genuine fatigue. Long gaming sessions often meant tired thumbs, highlighting a control logic that felt increasingly outdated compared to modern gaming standards.

Now, according to the latest details, the control scheme is receiving a much-needed modern update. In GTA 6, players will no longer have to endure the finger-numbing button mashing. Instead, the mechanic has been streamlined: now you press L3 to run.

### A Welcome Quality-of-Life Improvement

Transitioning to the left-stick click (L3) for sprinting brings the franchise in line with modern action-adventure standards. This intuitive change allows for smoother combat movement, easier exploration, and an overall more comfortable gameplay experience. While players wait for more deep dives into the game's mechanics, this small yet significant quality-of-life update proves that developer choices are continuing to evolve alongside player expectations.

## Editor's Take

Throwing away the mandatory X-mashing to run is arguably one of the best quality-of-life upgrades GTA 6 could possibly make. It removes a tedious physical hurdle, letting us enjoy the streets of Vice City without destroying our controllers. It is a small change, but a massively appreciated one.
